title: Guitar company D’Addario admits that AI music was used in a promotional video
slides: D’Addario's ad hides AI music, but why now?
The video celebrates human artistry, not machines.
Musicians unknowingly heard synthetic strings in endorsement.
Artists must now question every branded audio contract.
Disclose AI involvement in your next promo immediately.
thread_text:
1. The hidden AI track

D’Addario’s latest ad features synthetic strings, but the musicians endorsing it didn’t know. They only heard the final mix—and it wasn’t human.

2. The irony of the message

The video’s narration celebrates human artistry, yet the audio behind those words was machine-made. It’s a contradiction that undermines the entire campaign.

3. The contract loophole

Most branded audio deals don’t specify AI use, leaving artists exposed. That’s why the musicians couldn’t object—their contracts never covered it.

4. The trust fallout

Once the truth surfaces, every past endorsement gets questioned. Artists now realize that their name can be attached to AI without consent.

5. Check your next promo

Before signing that audio contract, ask: does it disclose AI? If not, demand a clause. It’s the only way to protect your reputation.

instagram.caption:
The guitar strings you just heard in that D’Addario promo weren’t played by anyone. The musicians endorsing it found out after signing—the final mix was synthetic.

The video’s narration glorifies human artistry while the audio track is machine-made. The contracts these artists signed never mentioned AI, so there was no legal ground to object. That’s the loophole.

For anyone creating branded content, your name can now be attached to AI without your knowledge. Before your next endorsement, demand a written clause that discloses AI involvement in the audio.

Would you sign a deal today without that protection? 🎸🤖📝
